texts.preamble: Kanchansingh vs Nagar Palik Nigam on 5 September, 2017 -1- M.Cr.C No.4530/2017 05.09.2017:
texts.facts: Facts in brief are that the petitioners are Directors of 'Hotel Kalinga'. On 29.08.2009 at about 1.30 P.M complainant R.M.Jaiswal, Food Inspector, visited the hotel premises and collected samples of Mum's brand soybean sauce. On analysis the sample was found to be adulterated. After completing necessary formalities charge sheet was filed before the trial Court who after framing charges against the petitioners along with co-accused persons proceeded further. The trial is still pending before the learned trial Court. 3. During trial the petitioners submitted an application before the trial Court under section 17(2) of the Act of 1954 stating that they are being prosecuted being Directors of the Hotel Kalinga while they have nominated one Ravi Shivhare s/o Tularam Shivhare as nominee vide resolution passed by the company at their Board of Directors' meeting held on 03.08.2008 at Hotel Kalinga to be in-charge and responsible for conduct of business of the hotel. The application was dismissed by the trial Court observing that the case is being proceeded as summon trial. Charges have already been framed, therefore, in view of the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court passed in the case of Adalat Prasad vs. Roopram Jindal reported in 2004 (4) MPLJ 1(SC) the accused cannot be discharged once cognizance has been taken against him. 4. The petitioners challenged this order by filing revision. The application was opposed before the revisional Court on the ground that after receiving the report of the Public Analyst several letters have been sent to the owners/partners/Directors and other concerned persons of the hotel asking them to reveal the name of the nominee, if any, but no information was provided by the concerned persons , therefore, it appears that to avoid prosecution the petitioners have fabricated the nomination letter after 14 months of filing of the charge sheet before the trial Court. the trial Court on 12.04.2010 and submitted an application for sending second sample to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis but did not file any application under section 17(2) of the Act of 1954. Second sample got damaged during transition. The petitioners then filed an application for sending third sample to the Central Food Laboratory. With this application for the first time they file an application under section 17(2) of the Act of 1954.
texts.arguments: The petitioners appeared before Kanchansingh vs Nagar Palik Nigam on 5 September, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85674286/ 1 The objection was raised that this is a forged and fabricated document, therefore, it requires enquiry which is not possible without taking evidence. Learned revisional Court further considered that the petitioners may prove this document during their defence that prior to filing the charge sheet they have nominated a particular person authorizing him to look after the business of the company and dismissed the revision petition. 5. Learned counsel for the petitioners have come before this Court stating that the order of the revisional Court is contrary to the facts and record of the case. Learned Court has failed to consider and appreciate the provisions of section 17(2) of the Act of 1954 in right perspective. The revisional Court did not consider the fact that petitioners were not present on the spot at the time of taking samples by the complainant. They are not concerned with the day to day business of the company. They have been impleaded merely because they were Directors of the company. The company has already appointed a nominee under section 17(2) of the Act of 1954 and the said nominee has already been made as accused in the charge sheet. They ought not to have been impleaded as accused persons. Learned revisional Court also failed to appreciate the citation of the Apex Court in the case of R. Banerjee and others vs. H.D Dubey and others reported in 1992 (1) Prevention of Food Adulteration Cases 128 in which it is held that where the nominee is appointed by the company, the Directors of the company shall not be proceeded against, therefore, they prayed that the impugned order be [LEAKAGE_MASK] and they may be exonerated from prosecution. 6. In reply learned counsel for the respondent has submitted that respondent had sent various letters to the petitioner asking them to reveal the name of the nominee, if any, appointed by the company but the petitioners did not reply the same. The petitioners appeared before the trial Court on 12.04.2010. They did not file any application at the time of appearance denying all the facts stated by the petitioners. Learned counsel for the respondent has relied upon the observations of the revisional Court and prayed for dismissal of the petition. In that state of facts, the impugned order Kanchansingh vs Nagar Palik Nigam on 5 September, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85674286/ 2 does not appear to be illegal, incorrect or perverse which calls for interference by this Court in exercise of its inherent powers conferred under section 482 of the Cr.P.C. 9.
